[[File:Douglas C. Wallace.jpg|thumb|Douglas C. Wallace at the Benjamin Franklin Life Sciences Medal Symposium]]
'''Douglas Cecil Wallace''' (born November 6, 1946) is a [[geneticist]] and [[evolutionary biology|evolutionary biologist]] at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] and the [[Children's Hospital of Philadelphia]] in [[Pennsylvania]].<ref name=UPenn>{{cite web|title=Douglas C Wallace|url=https://www.med.upenn.edu/apps/faculty/index.php/g275/p8415634|publisher=The Trustees of the University of Pennsylvania|access-date=25 February 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Douglas C Wallace, PhD: Bio|url=https://www.chop.edu/doctors/wallace-douglas-c.html|publisher=The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia|access-date=25 February 2013}}</ref> He pioneered the use of [[human mitochondrial genetics|human mitochondrial DNA]] as a [[molecular marker]].

==Career==
Wallace earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] in [[Genetics]] and [[Developmental Biology]] at [[Cornell University]] in [[Ithaca, New York]] in 1968, a [[Master of Philosophy]] in [[Microbiology]] and [[Human Genetics]] at [[Yale University]] in [[New Haven, Connecticut]] in 1972 and a [[Ph.D.]] in Microbiology and Human Genetics at [[Yale University]] in 1975.<ref name=UPenn/> His dissertation was titled ''Cytoplasmic genetics in mammalian tissue culture cells''.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Wallace DC|year=1976|title=Cytoplasmic inheritance in mammalian tissue culture cells|display-authors=etal|pmid=1035581|volume=12|issue=11|journal=In Vitro|pages=758–76|doi=10.1007/bf02835451|s2cid=3245970}}</ref>

He remained at Yale University as a [[postdoctoral research|postdoctoral fellow]] until he was awarded a [[professor]]ship (''[[Professors in the United States#Assistant professor|Assistant Professor]]'') at the [[Stanford University School of Medicine]] in [[Stanford, California]] in 1976. In 1983 he became professor (''[[Professors in the United States#Adjunct professor|Adjunct Professor]]'') for [[Biochemistry]], [[Anthropology]] and [[Pediatrics]] (Genetics) at [[Emory University]] in [[Atlanta|Atlanta, Georgia]]. From 1996 to 2002, he was Chairperson and Senior Editor of the Mitochondrial DNA Locus-Specific Database for the [[Human Genome Organisation]] (HUGO). In 2002 he assumed a professorship of [[Molecular Genetics]] at the [[University of California, Irvine]] where he founded the Center for Molecular and Mitochondrial Medicine and Genetics. In 2006 he was awarded a [[Visiting scholar|visiting professorship]] at [[Academia Sinica]] in [[Taipei]], [[Taiwan]]. In 2010 he became professor of [[Pathology]] and [[Medical laboratory|Laboratory Medicine]] at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in [[Philadelphia]] and became the founding director of the Center for Mitochondrial and Epigenomic Medicine at the [[Children's Hospital of Philadelphia]].<ref name=GruberBio/><ref>{{cite web|title=Douglas C. Wallace to Join UCI Faculty in Biology and Medicine|url=http://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/news/article/4098|date=18 March 2002|publisher=UC|quote=Founder of 'Mitochondrial Eve' Research to Establish Molecular and Mitochondrial Medicine Center at Irvine|access-date=28 February 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130420044442/http://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/news/article/4098|archive-date=20 April 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Douglas C. Wallace, Ph.D. (CV)|url=http://www.phys.sinica.edu.tw/~tywufund/download/camp/2009/cv/cv_camp2009_DouglasC.Wallace.pdf|publisher=Institute of Physics, [[Academia Sinica]]|access-date=27 February 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Top Expert on Mitochondrial Disorders Launches Center at Children's Hospital|url=https://www.newswise.com/articles/top-expert-on-mitochondrial-disorders-launches-center-at-children-s-hospital|access-date=25 February 2013|newspaper=Newswise, Inc|date=28 October 2010}}</ref>

In June 2022 he was awarded an [[honorary degree]] in Medicine and Surgery by the [[University of Padua]], [[Italy]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2022-05-30 |title=The Honorary Degree for Douglas Cecil Wallace |url=https://800anniunipd.it/en/event/laurea-honorem-wallace/ |access-date=2023-07-05 |website=800 anni unipd |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Work==
Wallace is a pioneer in the study of [[mitochondrial DNA]]. Wallace and his colleagues introduced [[human mitochondrial genetics]] into the field of [[molecular genetics]].<ref name=Expanded>{{cite web|title=Douglas C Wallace, PhD: Expanded Bio|url=https://www.chop.edu/doctors/wallace-douglas-c.html?view=2|publisher=The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia|access-date=27 February 2013}}</ref> In 1975, Wallace was the first to associate a genetic disorder with a specific mitochondrial DNA region (resistance to [[chloramphenicol]]),<ref>{{cite journal|author=Wallace DC|title=Cytoplasmic transfer of chloramphenicol resistance in human tissue culture cells|year=1975|display-authors=etal|pmc=2109574|pmid=1176530|volume=67|journal=J Cell Biol|issue=1|pages=174–88|doi=10.1083/jcb.67.1.174}}</ref> and in 1990 he described a mitochondrial DNA mutation as the cause of a particular form of [[myoclonic epilepsy]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Shoffner JM|title=Myoclonic epilepsy and ragged-red fiber disease (MERRF) is associated with a mitochondrial DNA tRNA(Lys) mutation|year=1990|display-authors=etal|pmid=2112427|volume=61|issue=6|journal=Cell|pages=931–7|doi=10.1016/0092-8674(90)90059-n|s2cid=6101099}}</ref> He has been instrumental in the study of the [[Human genome#Mitochondrial DNA|mitochondrial genome]] and has developed new methods for the analysis of mitochondrial DNA.<ref name=Passano/>

Wallace and his colleagues demonstrated that human mitochondrial DNA is inherited exclusively from the mother<ref>{{cite journal|author=Giles RE|title=Maternal inheritance of human mitochondrial DNA|year=1980|display-authors=etal|pmid=6256757|pmc=350359|volume=77|issue=11|journal=Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A.|pages=6715–9|doi=10.1073/pnas.77.11.6715|bibcode=1980PNAS...77.6715G|doi-access=free}}</ref> and they reconstructed the origin and ancient migration patterns of women using variations in mitochondrial DNA sequences.<ref name=GruberBio/><ref name=Expanded/><ref>{{cite journal|author=Torroni A|title=Asian affinities and continental radiation of the four founding Native American mtDNAs|year=1993|display-authors=etal|pmc=1682412|pmid=7688932|volume=53|journal=Am J Hum Genet|issue=3|pages=563–90}} The term ''[[haplogroup]]'' was coined in this paper.</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Wallace DC|title=Mitochondrial DNA variation in human evolution and disease|year=1999|display-authors=etal|pmid=10570998|volume=238|journal=Gene|issue=1|pages=211–30|doi=10.1016/s0378-1119(99)00295-4}}</ref>
